# /[[dev-update-docs]]

Usage:

- /[[dev-update-docs]] — run the full four-phase refresh end-to-end. No
  arguments.

Project context:

- The docs site lives at `<docs_site>/` (Astro Starlight, npm-managed).
- Hand-written pages: `<docs_site>/src/content/docs/index.md`,
  `<docs_site>/src/content/docs/architecture/*.md`,
  `<docs_site>/src/content/docs/roadmap.md`, `<docs_site>/src/content/docs/changelog.md`.
- Auto-generated pages live under `<docs_site>/src/content/docs/reference/` and
  `<docs_site>/src/content/docs/glossary.md`. Humans **never** edit these — only
  `sdlc docs generate site` writes them.
- Source of truth for the reference pages: the skill vault notes
  `tooling/plugin/plugins/sdlc/skills/<name>/<name>.md`,
  `tooling/lib/model/entities/*/schema.ts`, the op registry
  (`tooling/lib/registry.ts`). Source of truth for the site glossary:
  `docs/planning/terms/`.
- The hand-written pages cite things like skill names, entity-type names,
  and op paths. When the plugin moves, those citations drift. Phase 2
  is the LLM-shaped check for that drift.

This skill is the only thing that touches the auto-generated reference
pages. If you're tempted to hand-edit a file under
`<docs_site>/src/content/docs/reference/` or `<docs_site>/src/content/docs/glossary.md`,
stop — edit the source under `tooling/` (or a term entity under
`docs/planning/terms/`) and re-run this skill.

## 1. Run the deterministic site generator

From the repo root, run:

```text
bun run tooling/cli/sdlc.ts docs generate site
```

The generator prints one line per page created, updated, or removed. Capture
the output for the final report. The generator is idempotent — running it
twice produces no diff — and explicitly deletes pages whose source has
vanished (loudly logged).

If the command exits non-zero, surface the error to the user and stop.
Do not proceed to the semantic verify in Phase 2.

## 2. Semantic drift check against the hand-written pages

The hand-written pages live under `<docs_site>/supplemental/` — `index.md`, the
four `architecture/*.md` (overview, deterministic-first, harness-agnostic,
github-ref-leases, plus the self-documenting `site-assembly.md`), and
`changelog.md`. (`roadmap.md` and the `architecture/data-model.md` page are
now **generated** from entities — they are not hand-written and not verified
here; the generator owns their accuracy.) These supplemental pages make
factual claims about the plugin: which skills it ships, which entity types
are schematized, which scripts exist, what version the plugin is at. Walk
each page and check those claims against the live source.

Edit the supplemental **source** under `<docs_site>/supplemental/` — never the
mirrored copy in the content root (the generator overwrites it).

### What to check for

For each hand-written page, look for:

- **Skill names cited** (`/sdlc:<name>`, `task-work`, `backlog-triage`, etc.). For each, confirm
  `tooling/plugin/plugins/sdlc/skills/<name>/<name>.md` exists.
- **Entity types cited** (`task`, `milestone`, `epic`, `backlog`). For
  each, confirm `tooling/lib/model/entities/<name>/schema.ts` exists.
- **Script names cited** (`start_task.ts`, `dedup_search.ts`, etc.).
  For each, confirm `tooling/scripts/<name>` or
  `tooling/plugin/plugins/sdlc/skills/*/<name>` exists.
- **Version numbers** — `v0.1.1` etc. — should match the plugin note
  `tooling/plugin/plugins/sdlc/sdlc.md`'s `ap-version` field.
- **Counts** ("the plugin currently ships N skills") — compare against
  the actual count of skill dirs under `tooling/plugin/plugins/sdlc/skills/`.
- **Concept names from the README** — "harness-agnostic",
  "deterministic-first" — confirm the README and `PRINCIPLES.md` still
  use the same vocabulary.

### How to act on findings

For each drift item, decide:

- **Fix in place.** A mechanical update — e.g. a missing skill name in
  a list, an outdated count, a stale version string. Use Edit to
  correct, then continue.
- **Flag to the user.** A semantic shift — e.g. a paragraph describing
  a workflow that no longer matches the SKILL.md procedure. Don't
  silently rewrite prose; surface the discrepancy with the file path
  and the specific claim, and ask via AskUserQuestion whether to
  attempt a rewrite, skip, or stop.
- **Note in the report.** A minor inconsistency that doesn't merit
  user intervention — e.g. a link target that resolves but feels
  awkward. Record it in the report; don't block.

Keep the bar high: this phase is about factual drift, not style. Do not
rewrite prose to taste.

## 3. Run the site build

Once regen has run and the hand-written pages are reconciled (or
flagged), run the same command Cloudflare uses on deploy:

```text
bun run build:doc-site
```

This installs deps (root + `<docs_site>/`), regenerates the site content, and
runs `astro build` — confirming Astro can render every page including
the regenerated reference. (It re-runs `docs generate site` from Step 2;
that is idempotent.) If the build fails:

- Read the error carefully — Starlight errors usually cite the offending
  file and frontmatter field.
- If the cause is a stray hand-written page (bad frontmatter, broken
  link), surface to the user and stop. Do not auto-rewrite.
- If the cause is something in the generator output, that's a bug in
  `tooling/lib/services/docs/site.ts` — flag the file and the parse
  failure to the user.

## 4. Report

Emit a single readable summary covering:

- **Regen** — what was created / updated / removed (or "no changes").
- **Drift** — what was fixed in place, what was flagged for the user,
  what was noted.
- **Build** — pass / fail; if fail, the cited file.
- **Where the build artifact lives** — typically `<docs_site>/dist/`.

Keep the report compact. The user reads this between other work.

## Notes

- This skill is repo tooling — it lives in this repo's `dev-agent` plugin
  (`content/agent-vault/`), not in the sdlc skill vault under
  `tooling/plugin/plugins/sdlc/skills/`. It's not part of the distributed sdlc
  plugin. It exists to keep this repo's own docs honest.
- The whole content root under `<docs_site>/src/content/docs/` is generated —
  reference pages, entity rosters + child pages, glossary/references, the
  data-model and roadmap pages, and the sidebar — but **gitignored and not
  committed**: Cloudflare rebuilds it on deploy (`sdlc docs generate site`
  then `astro build`, via `bun run build:doc-site`). The only hand-written
  prose is the supplemental set under `<docs_site>/supplemental/` (landing,
  architecture, changelog), mirrored into the content root by the site
  pass. This skill verifies that supplemental prose against the live
  plugin. The `verbs.check` gate no longer diffs the site; it
  build-validates it (`sdlc docs generate site` throws on structural
  breakage), while `sdlc docs generate --check` covers only the committed
  wiki artifacts. How the whole assembly works is documented on the site
  itself at `/architecture/site-assembly/` (source
  `<docs_site>/supplemental/architecture/site-assembly.md`).
- If `npm --prefix site dev` is running in another terminal while this
  skill runs, the dev server will hot-reload as files change. That's
  fine and expected.
